subject: RE: Northbridge - data residency conditionalities & activation window
messages:
From: Emma Wilson <emma.wilson@northbridgebank.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@northbridgebank.com
Date: 2027-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data residency constraints and transient caching question

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our internal RFP compliance checks we need a concise mapping of how Redwood would meet our data residency constraints. Key points we need confirmed for Northbridge:

- Primary customer data (customer PII and transaction indices) must be persisted and processed within the EU (Ireland) at all times.
- Transient caches / KV layers used for inference MAY be hosted outside the EU only under strict conditions and only for disaster-recovery activation windows. If permitted, the maximum TTL for any outside-EU cached data must be stated.
- BYOK / HSM usage: does Redwood support EU-keyed HSMs such that keys never leave EU KMS?
- Telemetry / logs: what telemetry is collected, where is it stored, and retention period (we require audit logs retained for 12 months in EU).
- Evidence: SOC2 report, network topology, and a short bullet list of technical controls we can attach to our SOC/Legal review.

Can you provide a short written statement and any attachments we can put in our compliance packet? Also share an estimate for how long it would take to operationalize the EU-only hosting constraints for an initial POC.

Best,
Emma Wilson
Director, Cloud Risk & Compliance
Northbridge Bank

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wilson <emma.wilson@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: procurement@northbridgebank.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Data residency constraints and transient caching question

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. Summary answers up front, followed by the technical commitments and a proposed mutual action plan. Attached: NB_Sovereignty_Q_Responses_v2.pdf and redwood-eu-network-topology.png for your packet.

Short summary (high level):
1) Primary storage & processing: We will commit to storing and processing persisted customer data within the EU (Ireland) for the Northbridge contract. This applies to both Hosted and Dedicated modes when EU pinning is requested.
2) Transient caches: By default Redwood configures prefix/KV caches inside the same region as model execution. For Northbridge we will:
   - Default: EU-only caches (no cross-border cache by default).
   - Disaster Recovery exception: we can agree to an activation window where ephemeral caches spin up in a secondary region outside the EU (e.g., us-east) only while failover is active. Any outside-EU cache would be encrypted with customer-managed EU keys and have a maximum TTL of 24 hours unless explicitly extended with written approval.
3) BYOK / HSM: We support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and can connect to EU HSM/KMS so keys do not leave EU control. We also support bring-your-own-HSM for Private deployments.
4) Telemetry & logs: Application telemetry is pseudonymized by default; audit logs (access, deployment, routing decisions) can be retained in an EU log store for 12 months. We provide periodic export in a vendor-neutral format.

Technical commitments & controls (brief):
- All persisted data for Northbridge instances will be stored on EU-region volumes with at-rest encryption (AES-256).
- Network egress from EU processing hosts is blocked by default; any approved egress (e.g., to a DR cache) requires a documented activation request and automated egress logging.
- Ephemeral caches outside the EU are built on encrypted volumes and are configured for automatic flush on deactivation; key material remains in EU KMS.
- Telemetry: collection minimized to routing metadata and anonymized service metrics; PII redaction pipelines in place.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II (most recent report) and network topology diagram attached.

Proposed mutual action plan (timeline):
- Day 0–7: Sign confidentiality and standard SOW; confirm EU pinning and BYOK preference.
- Day 7–21: Provision Dedicated/EU-hosted environment, integrate customer KMS (if BYOK selected), deploy initial POC models.
- Day 21–35: Run test scripts for residency/egress proofing, deliver audit artifacts.

We can also prepare a short SLA amendment that enumerates the DR activation window terms (TTL, key controls, logging requirements).

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute technical call with Marcus (solutions) and Laura (enterprise sales engineering) to walk through the topology and the attachments.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: NB_Sovereignty_Q_Responses_v2.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-eu-network-topology.png (image/png)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-12T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Data residency constraints and transient caching question — need approval for DR exception

Ben/Laura/Marcus — forwarding Northbridge's request and our proposed language (attached). They have a hard audit window and asked for the DR activation allowance (outside-EU caches, max TTL).

Proposed commercial mitigation: offer a 1-month hosting credit in exchange for the documented DR exception and the SLA amendment that requires immediate cache purge and EU KMS encryption on activation.

Technical mitigations we will enforce if approved:
- Activation requires an authorized runbook trigger (multi-signer via customer SRE + Redwood on-call).
- All activation events are logged and shipped to customer EU log store.
- Automatic cache flush TTL enforcement and a post-activation attestation report.

Can I get sign-off to proceed with drafting the SLA amendment and agreeing to the 24-hour TTL for DR caches (with the one-month credit)? Legal will still need to sign off but we want to be clear with the customer.

Thanks,
Jasmine

- Legal sign-off required on the SLA amendment (Laura please coordinate).
- Add an SLA credit cap tied to the activation frequency (e.g., credits only for first activation per quarter unless otherwise negotiated).

Progress with drafting the amendment and I will flag the concession to the AE desk. Marcus, please prepare a short checklist of technical attestation items we will deliver post-activation.

—Ben
VP Sales Operations
